one_liner: Write, profile, and optimize custom CUDA kernels (tiled matmul, fused ops) for LLM workloads.

key_terms.definition: NVIDIA's parallel programming framework in which host code on the CPU launches device code (kernels) that run on thousands of GPU threads.
A group of 32 threads that execute the same instruction in lockstep on a GPU's functional units (the SIMT model); the basic scheduling unit.
When threads in the same warp take different branch paths, forcing the hardware to execute both paths sequentially with inactive threads masked, halving throughput.
The physical GPU core that executes a thread block, holding many concurrent warps and hiding memory-load latency by switching to a ready warp.
The ratio of active warps per SM to the SM's maximum warp capacity; a proxy for how well memory latency is hidden, though not the only performance factor.
The hardware's combining of a warp's global-memory accesses into as few 128-byte transactions as possible, achieved when threads read consecutive addresses.
Serialized (slowed) memory access that occurs when multiple threads in a warp read different addresses that map to the same one of shared memory's 32 banks; fixed by padding array rows.
CUDA primitives (`__shfl_sync`, `__shfl_down_sync`, `__shfl_xor_sync`) that let threads within a warp exchange register values directly, without shared memory or `__syncthreads()`.
A matmul strategy where each thread block cooperatively loads T×T sub-tiles of A and B into shared memory and reuses them, cutting global memory reads by a factor of T versus the naive kernel.
The ratio of FLOPs performed to bytes read from memory, used with the roofline model to determine whether a kernel is compute-bound or memory-bound.
Specialized GPU hardware that executes fused mixed-precision matrix-multiply-accumulate operations (via `wmma`/`mma` instructions) at much higher throughput than standard FMA units.
A CUDA synchronization primitive that blocks every thread in a block from proceeding until all threads have reached it, preventing read/write hazards on shared memory.
